payload.name: Preserve Explicit Activity Formats in Enrichment
payload.description: When a message describes a hobby or activity with emotional significance and explicitly names concrete formats, outlets, or instances (e.g., journal, blog post), during extraction or enrichment.
content: During extraction, when a message ties an activity to a general feeling (e.g., 'writing is my rock') and explicitly names concrete forms or outlets (e.g., a journal, an online blog post), capture each named form as a distinct facet in the profile/preference/event memory; do not collapse the candidate into only the emotional significance.
When enriching an existing memory about the activity, preserve previously stored facets and ADD the newly named concrete forms rather than replacing the memory with a narrower paraphrase.

Before SKIPping a candidate that mentions a specific instance (e.g., a blog post) because a related general memory exists, verify that the specific fact is already present; if not, add or merge it. Stop after capturing only the explicitly named forms; do not infer unstated ones.

candidates.solves: Extraction often keeps only the emotional summary of an activity and drops explicitly named concrete forms (e.g., journal, blog post), so later questions about what the person actually does are unanswerable.

payload.name: Extract Explicit Feelings in Reflective Memories
payload.description: When a user explicitly names emotions or feelings (e.g., peace, gratitude, joy) tied to a memory, place, or person, include those stated feelings in the extracted memory content.
content: During extraction, when a message contains a first-person reflective statement about a past experience, place, or person and explicitly states the feelings it evokes (e.g., 'I feel peace and gratitude'), include those exact feelings in the candidate memory content alongside the factual details.
Capture only feelings explicitly stated by the speaker; do not infer or add unmentioned emotions.
Use the same rule when updating or enriching an existing memory: if the message adds feelings about a previously stored memory, merge them into the existing memory content.
Stop after recording the stated feelings; do not expand the memory with extra details or searches.

candidates.solves: Construction extraction often records the factual content of a reflective memory (activity, place, companion) but omits the emotions the speaker explicitly says the memory evokes, so later questions about feelings cannot be answered. This skill ensures explicitly stated feelings are preserved in memory content during extraction and updates.

payload.name: Extract Detailed Past Events with Time Anchors
payload.description: When a user narrates a specific past experience with a time anchor such as 'last week' or 'yesterday', during extraction create an event memory for that occurrence, even if the message also expresses feelings or preferences.
content: During extraction, if a message narrates a concrete past event the speaker experienced (e.g., an outing, sighting, visit, or occurrence) and includes a relative or absolute time anchor, create a separate event memory capturing the activity, key details, and timing resolved from the message/session timestamp; do not fold it only into a preference, state, or comfort-source memory.
If the same message also contains emotional or supportive content, still emit the event candidate separately from any comfort/joy source memory.
Record only explicitly stated factual details; do not infer unmentioned participants, places, or outcomes. Emit at most one event per distinct occurrence and stop once the event is captured.

candidates.solves: This solves the failure to persist concrete past events that users mention in casual conversation, especially when those messages also contain emotional or preference language. Without this rule, such events are omitted because the extractor focuses on feelings or other memory types, leaving future questions about what/when unanswered.

payload.name: Extract Explicit Facts from Emotional Statements
payload.description: Use during extraction when a message pairs an emotional or preference statement with an explicit factual assertion, such as a specific date, event, or relationship detail.
content: During extraction, if a message contains both an emotional/preference statement and an explicit factual assertion (e.g., 'This is my parents' wedding in 1993'), create a separate candidate for the factual assertion in addition to any preference candidate.

Record explicit dates/events as an event or relationship memory (e.g., 'Deborah's parents married in 1993') with the year in the content and world_start instead of embedding the fact only in a general preference.
Extract only facts explicitly stated; stop once the distinct assertions are captured and do not infer unmentioned dates or details.

candidates.solves: When construction extraction collapses a message that mixes feelings with concrete facts, it loses answerable facts like dates of past events. This skill ensures explicit factual assertions in narrative or emotional messages are extracted as their own durable memory.

payload.name: Preserve All Explicit Actions in Compound Event Memories
payload.description: When a message states an event with multiple explicit actions or activities (e.g., 'reminisced and looked through photos'), during extraction and CRUD, ensure every explicitly stated action is preserved.
content: During extraction, when a speaker describes an event using multiple explicit actions connected by 'and', 'also', or 'plus', create one event candidate that records every stated action; do not let a visually salient action like sharing photos replace or subsume other explicit actions such as reminiscing.
Include the participants explicitly stated for the activity (e.g., 'with her mom's old friends') when the message or immediate context provides them.
During UPDATE or MERGE, when enriching an event memory, compare the proposed version against the source message and preserve all originally stated actions; do not drop any action while adding detail.

candidates.solves: Construction extraction often collapses a compound activity to the most salient action (e.g., photo sharing) and drops other explicitly stated actions such as reminiscing, causing incomplete event memories that fail later reference checks. This skill ensures all explicit actions and participants in a stated event are preserved.

payload.name: Extract explicit duration facts from dialogue
payload.description: When a speaker states a concrete duration or span for a past activity, membership, or relationship (e.g., 'teammates for four years'), and the fact appears in conversation or as an answer to a question.
content: During extraction, if a speaker states a concrete duration or span for a past activity, membership, or relationship (e.g., 'We were teammates for four years in high school'), create a candidate memory capturing that fact, even when the statement answers a question or occurs in small talk.
Record who was involved, what the activity or relationship was, and the exact stated duration; use an event or state memory and resolve relative time from the message timestamp when needed.
Do not infer unstated durations or extend the fact to other activities; stop once the stated duration is captured.

candidates.solves: Construction sometimes fails to extract explicitly stated facts about how long a person participated in an activity, membership, or relationship, especially when the fact is stated conversationally or as an answer to a question. This causes missing memories that are needed later for duration questions.

payload.name: Preserve Explicit Emotional Takeaways in Event Memories
payload.description: When a user narrates a past event and explicitly states an emotional response or what the event meant to them (e.g., relief, love, gratitude).
content: During extraction, when a user narrates a past event and explicitly states how it felt or what it meant ('so relieved', 'showed how much I love her'), include that emotional or reflective statement in the event candidate rather than summarizing only the factual sequence.
Preserve the user's own framing of the event's significance even when it appears in a longer anecdote; do not strip subjective clauses as non-facts.

During CRUD, if an existing event memory for the same event lacks an explicitly stated emotional takeaway from the same message, UPDATE or MERGE the memory to add it instead of creating a duplicate. Do not infer feelings that are not explicitly stated.

candidates.solves: When users share personal anecdotes, their explicitly stated feelings or the meaning they drew from the event are durable facts, but summary-style extraction often omits them, leaving memory unable to answer feeling-oriented questions.

payload.name: Capture All Explicitly Stated Experience Aspects
payload.description: When a message describes an event, session, or experience as being about multiple named aspects, use during extraction to preserve each one.
content: During extraction, when a speaker describes an event, session, or experience as being about multiple explicitly named aspects (e.g., 'about releasing expectations and judgments and just savoring the present'), include every named aspect in the memory content.
Do not paraphrase the experience in a way that drops any explicitly stated component; preserve the full set of stated topics even if one seems more prominent.
Stop after capturing all explicitly named aspects; do not infer additional themes or details beyond what was stated.

candidates.solves: Prevents incomplete extraction of conjunctive descriptions, ensuring memories retain all explicitly stated components of an experience and later questions about any component can be answered.

payload.name: Preserve Temporal Links Between Related Events
payload.description: Use during extraction when a message refers back to a previously mentioned person, event, or activity (e.g., 'that fan I met', 'reconnected') and the earlier mention exists in the session or memory pool.
content: During extraction, if a message refers back to a previously mentioned person, event, or activity, search the current session and existing memories for the earlier mention before finalizing the candidate.

When the earlier mention is found, record the connection in the new event memory, including the elapsed time between the two events computed from their timestamps (e.g., 'reconnected with X three weeks after first meeting X').
If the exact interval cannot be computed, store the dates of both events and the fact of the reconnection without inventing a number.
Stop after capturing the link and interval; do not expand into unrelated details or add extra searches.

candidates.solves: Later messages often refer back to an earlier mentioned person, event, or activity without restating the relationship. Extracted memories then lose the connection and elapsed time, making temporal questions unanswerable. This skill ensures the later event memory captures the reference to the prior event and the interval between them.

payload.name: Preserve concrete activities in event memories
payload.description: When a message describes a personal experience with a specific activity or action and an emotional evaluation (e.g., 'so freeing to dance and bop around'), use during extraction to preserve the concrete action(s) in the event memory.
content: During extraction, when a message describes an event with a concrete activity or action (e.g., dancing, hiking, singing) and an emotional evaluation of it (e.g., freeing, magical, peaceful), include the concrete action(s) in the event memory content, in addition to the evaluation.
Do not reduce the event to only the emotional quality or a general summary; preserve the stated action so the memory records what the person actually did.
Only include actions the user explicitly mentions; do not infer unstated activities. Emit at most one memory containing the stated activity and evaluation per message.

candidates.solves: When messages describe an event alongside an emotional evaluation, extraction candidates may keep only the evaluation and omit the concrete action it refers to. This skill ensures event memories preserve explicit activities so later questions about what the person did or what they found freeing/joyful can be answered from the stored memory.

payload.name: Extract Stated Feelings from Past Events
payload.description: When a speaker describes a past event and explicitly states how it felt or describes the atmosphere/conditions, extract an event memory.
content: During extraction, treat a speaker's explicit description of how a past event felt (e.g., 'the atmosphere was electric', 'it felt great') as memory-worthy even when the message also contains encouragement or small talk.
Create one event memory for the described event that records the speaker, the event, and the stated feelings or atmospheric qualifiers using the speaker's own words.
Use the single message as sufficient evidence when the speaker is recounting their own experience; resolve relative time from the message/session timestamp.
Stop after the event and its stated feelings are captured; do not infer unmentioned emotions or expand into additional memory kinds.

candidates.solves: Construction often skips extraction when a speaker answers a question about feelings by narrating a past event, so explicit subjective facts like atmosphere, emotional reactions, and memorable conditions are never persisted. This creates gaps where later questions about how the speaker felt cannot be answered from memory.

payload.name: Extract Explicit Emotional States
payload.description: When a user explicitly states how they feel (e.g., discouraged, determined, excited) about an ongoing situation or activity, during extraction or CRUD.
content: During extraction, if a message explicitly states the speaker's emotional state about an ongoing situation (e.g., 'a bit discouraged but determined', 'excited about the move', 'worried about the deadline'), create a separate durable memory capturing that feeling in addition to any event or action memory.

Use memory kind 'state' for the emotional state, with the speaker as subject and the emotion words preserved verbatim where possible; include the object or context only if the message ties the feeling to it.
Do not infer or add emotions that are not explicitly stated; if the message contains both an action and a feeling, extract both rather than folding the feeling into the action memory.
Stop after capturing the stated emotional state; do not expand into broader personality traits or unrelated attitudes unless also explicitly stated.

During CRUD, when adding or updating a memory derived from a message that explicitly states an emotion, verify that the emotional state is represented; if missing, update the memory or add a separate state memory before completing the operation.

candidates.solves: When extraction summarizes an ongoing action (e.g., searching, moving, applying) but drops explicitly stated emotional states, later questions about how the person feels cannot be answered. This skill ensures explicit feelings are captured as durable state memories alongside action/event memories, and preserved during updates.

payload.name: Extract casual first-person past actions
payload.description: When a message contains a first-person statement about a concrete action performed in the past, even if phrased casually or embedded in a larger conversational turn.
content: During extraction, create an event memory candidate for any first-person statement describing a concrete past action (made, baked, cooked, tried, visited, attended, etc.), regardless of casual tone or surrounding conversational content.
Capture the action, the object or details (e.g., dessert with almond milk), and any time expression exactly as stated.
Resolve relative time expressions (e.g., last Friday) to an absolute date using the message/session timestamp, and store the resolved date in the memory content and metadata.
Stop after capturing the event; do not add extra details, feelings, or merge it into other candidates.

candidates.solves: During extraction, concrete first-person statements about past actions (e.g., 'I made a dessert with almond milk') are sometimes omitted when they appear in casual conversational messages, causing the fact to be absent from memory. This skill ensures these statements become event memory candidates and relative times are resolved to absolute dates.

payload.name: Extract Described Calming and Care Actions
payload.description: When a user explicitly states actions they took to calm, comfort, or care for a pet or other dependent after a stressful event, during extraction.
content: During extraction, if a user explicitly lists actions they performed to calm, comfort, or care for a pet or dependent after an incident, create one candidate memory capturing the target and those actions.
Use memory kind 'event' for the one-time response, or 'state' if the user frames it as a recurring care routine; record each action verb and its object.
Do not skip the candidate because the message also contains emotional or relational framing, and do not require a direct question—first-person reflective statements are sufficient evidence.
Create at most one candidate per described incident response; avoid splitting each action into separate memories.

candidates.solves: Construction sometimes drops first-person statements that list concrete actions taken to calm, comfort, or care for a pet or dependent after an incident, leaving no memory for later questions. This skill ensures such described action sequences are extracted as durable event/state candidates.

payload.name: Preserve Distinct Event Facts Alongside Opinions
payload.description: Use during extraction when a message mixes a general opinion, agreement, or sentiment with a specific personal event such as a past trip or activity.
content: When a message contains both a general opinion/agreement and a specific factual event (e.g., 'This was my ... trip last year'), extract the event as its own candidate memory rather than capturing only the sentiment.
Resolve relative time phrases like 'last year' from the message/session timestamp and record the resolved date on the event candidate.
Extract only the distinct claims explicitly stated; do not infer extra details, and stop once the opinion and the specific event are each captured as separate candidates.

candidates.solves: Construction extraction sometimes collapses a message that mixes an opinion or agreement with a specific personal experience, dropping the concrete event (e.g., a past trip) because the sentiment dominates. This Skill ensures each explicitly stated factual claim is preserved as its own candidate, with relative time resolved from the session timestamp.
